legend.PASS: Implemented AND proven by an executed command recorded in `evidence`.
legend.FAIL: Implemented but its acceptance check currently fails.
legend.BLOCKED: Cannot proceed until the named blocker clears.

rules: A capability is PASS only with executable evidence: a command that was actually run and its result.
Code existing is never sufficient for PASS. See docs/TESTING.md, Definition of Done.
`evidence.verified_at` must be null whenever status is not PASS.

capabilities.name: Declarative rule engine, hot-reloadable

evidence.result: pytest tests/unit/test_rules_*.py + tests/contract: 18 declarative YAML rules over the 26 declared features, one unit test per rule including the abstention path. Kleene three-valued logic (ADR-0033): an absent feature yields UNKNOWN and never FALSE, so a missing input cannot read as 'no risk'; UNKNOWN still settles where a false conjunct or true disjunct decides the outcome. Hot reload is atomic and fail-safe -- an invalid candidate leaves the previous pack in force and increments rule_pack_reload_failed_total. Noisy-OR scoring with band floors that only raise. Validated end to end by the eval-v1 replay: 12 distinct rules fired across 60,000 replayed transactions, R008 among them.

capabilities.name: Duplicate transaction_id yields one effect

evidence.result: pytest tests/integration/test_gateway_concurrency.py + test_triage_store.py: two tiers, and the authoritative one is the database. 32 concurrent retries of one logical request against a live gateway open exactly one case, one queue row and one outbox row -- the case that matters, because concurrent retries all miss the Redis replay cache before the first response is stored, leaving cases.trigger_transaction_id UNIQUE as the only thing preventing N investigations. Writing that test found a real defect: open_case minted its own case_id while the caller had already built investigation.requested.v1 with a different one, so every published event named a case that did not exist (191,455 outbox rows, zero matching). The caller's id is now authoritative and the assertion names the case rather than its shape.

capabilities.name: Gateway observation log: every crash, shed and outage loss is a detectable gap

evidence.result: 10 passed, in two consecutive runs on the fixed tree; with tests/chaos/test_outbox_watermark.py, 11 passed

capabilities.notes: Phase 3 Step 4 (ADR-0051, Proposed). Slice 1 (2026-09-14): migration 0006 app.producer_sessions (database-clock timestamps, immutable identity, close-once, column-scoped trace_app grants), PostgresSessionLedger, PostgresWriterLock (a session-scoped advisory lock that ends with its connection) and trace_core.observation.session.WriterSession (fenced start, contiguous sequences, loss on any unconfirmed heartbeat, close only on a confirmed flush), with unit tests and integration tests against PostgreSQL. Slice 2 (2026-09-14): the gateway behind the fence. WriterSupervisor (heartbeat every 2 s off the event loop, a 6 s lease so a stuck heartbeat cannot keep an instance writing, an 8 s takeover grace after an unclosed predecessor, re-acquisition with a new session), /readyz writer_session, 503 with Retry-After for scoring, feature-read identity events and authorization outcomes while not the writer, start-up online-state writes only inside the fence, writer_refused_total. Evidence: 93 unit, contract and integration tests passed with none skipped; pytest -m chaos tests/chaos/test_writer_fence.py 1 passed (a terminated writer backend; never two ready writers). Slice 3 (2026-09-14): tx.scored.v1 released with its producer (schema, RELEASED entry, codegen model, topics.py key, topics.yaml declaration replacing the reservation with a measured record size) and the observation log: trace_core.observation.scored_event and ObservationLog sequence every online-state write (scored transactions, identity events that feed a stream), write online, then produce with block=False and tracex-session-id/tracex-seq headers; a session closes only on a confirmed flush of every assigned number, and the slice-2 shutdown that closed sessions with nothing logged was fixed. Evidence: 606 targeted unit, contract, conformance and integration tests passed with none skipped; tests/integration/test_observation_log_kafka.py against a real broker 2 passed (contiguous numbers across both topics, LogAppendTime, keyed; a paused broker refuses the close). Slice 4 (2026-09-14): OutboxRelay (SKIP LOCKED batches marked published only on a confirmed flush; rows whose own content cannot be published refused once and skipped; delivery failures retried) and migration 0007 (outbox rows inserted unpublished, relayed content immutable, published_at stamped once, trace_app UPDATE narrowed to the relay columns), wired into the gateway behind TRACE_GATEWAY_OUTBOX_RELAY and off until the A/B. Evidence: 276 targeted tests passed with none skipped, including the PostgreSQL relay and guard suites and fresh-migration ground-truth isolation; tests/integration/test_outbox_relay_kafka.py against a real broker 2 passed. Slice 5 (2026-09-15): the coverage rule (trace_core.observation.coverage, 14 unit tests) and the chaos suite. Scope: the kills hit a child process composing the production writer, pipeline, Redis store and log between the calls the gateway makes; the gateway's route order is unit-tested, and killing the rebuilt gateway under load belongs with the A/B. Reverted from PASS (2026-09-15): an independent critic found two Category A defects in the coverage rule, both confirmed by reproduction. A live session read before a later loss got a gap ending before it starts, and a gap started at the previous record's arrival, which can be later than the lost write. The critic also found that the chaos checks could not fail. Fixed (2026-09-15): the rule bounds gaps by the writer's own stamps, and by the ledger and log read times. Nothing at or after Coverage.through is vouched for. An unclosed tail is bounded by the writer's lease and takeover margin. Hypothesis property tests generate histories. The chaos checks put every lost write's recorded time inside a gap of its session, and one case reads the ledger mid-run before a loss. B2: the gateway pool bounds acquire and statement time by POSTGRES_TIMEOUT_S, and the writer is re-checked before every store write. Its unit tests are mutation-checked, and PostgreSQL enforcement passed 2. B3: rows handed over before a retryable failure are confirmed and marked. Rows after it are deferred, with no attempt. Authorization-outcome delivery watermark (user decision, 2026-09-15): migration 0008; outbox_watermark.advance in the relay's marking transaction, on every pass; and history_completeness, COMPLETE only when observation coverage and the watermark both vouch. Evidence: pytest -m chaos tests/chaos/test_observation_log.py passed 10 in two consecutive runs. tests/chaos/test_outbox_watermark.py passed 1: a lost marking commit keeps history INCOMPLETE though Kafka holds the records, duplicates are re-delivered, and history is COMPLETE only after the marks. The relay, watermark and pool suites passed 21 against PostgreSQL and 4 against a real broker. 185 gateway, observation and coverage unit tests passed. Critic re-review of 1d216c5 (2026-09-15) found one Category A defect: the write check asked whether the process was the writer, not whether the session that numbered the observation still was, so after a same-process re-acquisition an old session's number passed. It is fixed with WriterSupervisor.ready_as(session_id), and the tests fail when the session is ignored. Also fixed: readiness now reports a dead relay thread; a clock offset within the margin is no longer an anomaly; vouches refuses while any anomaly stands. Chaos on the fixed tree passed 11. Rule mutation checks, 10 mutants: the hand-written coverage tests catch every mutant on every run. The widened property tests catch 22 of 30 mutant-seed runs; two margin mutants, the lease bound and through, survive every seed. The old property tests caught 2 of 30. Step 4 exit (2026-09-15): scripts/observation_log_ab.py report applied the pre-registered hot-path A/B as written (benchmarks/gateway/observation-log-ab.md). It rejected option A on achieved rate: log-relay was the faster arm, just outside a noise band the fixed offered rate makes tiny, and the rule compares absolute differences, so it stands. Scoring-core p99 was within noise. Three runs that failed integrity were recorded and repeated. Option B is implemented: services/worker/relay.py runs OutboxRelay in trace-worker (compose `worker`, streaming profile). tests/unit/test_worker_relay.py passed 5 and tests/integration/test_worker_relay_kafka.py passed 2.

capabilities.name: Sustained stream throughput and outage recovery at the 5,000 events/s target rate, recorded honestly
A wrong Java, Spark, Delta, Hadoop, Scala or jar fails fast with an actionable message

evidence.command: pytest tests/unit/test_stream_toolchain.py tests/unit/test_doctor.py tests/unit/test_toolchain_consistency.py && JAVA_HOME=$(python scripts/java_home.py) pytest -m stream tests/stream/test_session.py
evidence.result: Unit, no JVM (fake JDKs are real executables printing a JDK version banner): Java 25 refused with the JAVA_HOME fix, and the PATH fallback checked exactly as Spark's launcher resolves it; an installed pip at another version and an uninstalled distribution refused; Hadoop 3.3 and Scala 2.12 jars refused; one flipped bit in a locked jar refused; PYSPARK_SUBMIT_ARGS, SPARK_CONF_DIR and a foreign SPARK_HOME refused before any JVM; every failure listed in one ToolchainMismatchError; doctor FAILs (required) on Java 25 and on missing jars from Phase 3, refuses an unparseable phase, and exits non-zero when run under Java 25; an all-skipped `-m stream` session exits non-zero with the collection-guard message; every pip install in the Makefile, workflows, Dockerfiles and shell scripts is hash-checked or the project's own --no-deps install; every CI job installs from the lock before its tooling; the lock is complete for Linux x86_64, Linux aarch64 and macOS arm64; the gateway's runtime lock is exactly derived from the main lock. Real JVM on Temurin 17: a Spark 4.0.1 session reports Java 17, Scala 2.13.x and Hadoop 3.4.x from the running JVM; Delta's session extension and the Kafka source provider load from the SHA-256-verified jars; a Delta table round-trips at millisecond UTC event time; the Kafka connector resolves with no spark.jars.packages; an invalid cast raises under ANSI; a real installed Temurin 25 is refused in a fresh interpreter before pyspark.sql is imported; a JVM contradicting a pin is stopped and refused after launch. Linux: a hashed install of both locks in python:3.12-slim passes pip check, and the gateway image builds from its hashed runtime lock with pip check clean and no pyspark or pytest inside. Pending: the first GitHub CI run. ADR-0045.

capabilities.name: Local resource caps asserted; unsafe lake maintenance refused

evidence.command: pytest -m 'unit or integration' -k resource_bounds && pytest -m stream tests/stream/test_resource_bounds_maintenance.py
evidence.result: 46 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped in 59.51 s at commit 86d69e7 (the Step 11 landing, ADR-0052 Amendment 1): 44 unit cases and 2 integration cases against a throwaway Kafka broker, Postgres and Delta 4.0.1 on Temurin 17.0.20.1 (macOS, clean Docker environment). The same commit's Step 11 stream suite, marked `stream` only and so outside this command (debt D22), passed separately: `pytest -m stream tests/stream/test_resource_bounds_maintenance.py` 14 passed, 0 skipped in 409.15 s (crash at every maintenance step, refusals commit nothing, Bronze-only ignoreDeletes, Silver reset after retention, VACUUM/OPTIMIZE guards, an append racing maintenance). Hydration at the same commit: 11 passed. The first run of this command, on the pre-fix tree c4912d6, FAILED 1 of 44: a real broker's topic id contained '+', which the floor key refused; fixed in 86d69e7. Open: Amendment 1 Risks 1-3 (D21).
